title: structured output: constrained decoding backends (CFG / regex / tokenizer edgecases)
author: Asha Patel
description: Context: We need robust structured-output constrained decoding across multiple backends to support: (1) CFG/grammar-based constraints for strongly-typed outputs, (2) regex token-aware constraints for schema validation, and (3) correct handling of tokenizer edgecases (BPE / subword splits) when applying constraints. Motivation: Existing constrained-decoding code was tightly coupled to a single matcher implementation and failed on common tokenizer edgecases (e.g., partial token matches for anchors, multi-token regex matches, and whitespace-sensitive CFG productions). This caused downstream failures in the OpenAI-compat layer where users rely on deterministic structured outputs for tools/function-calling workflows. Summary of changes: - Add a new pluggable constrained-decoding backend interface and implement three matchers: cfg_backend (Python), regex_backend (Rust -> FFI), tokenizer-aware matcher that defers to the runtime tokenization model to align constraint spans. - CFG backend: supports grammar productions expressed in a slim DSL, fast first-match pruning, and deterministic expansion ordering required for canary rollouts. - Regex backend: introduces a token-aware regex engine that compiles regexes to a token-level DFA; handles lookaround by mapping to token boundaries and supports common regex anchors when token boundaries cross subword splits. - Tokenizer fixes: central fixes to BPE handling so constraints operate on normalized token sequences (handles leading/trailing spaces, shared prefixes across tokens, and unicode normalizations). Added explicit mapping utilities so backends can translate between characters, codepoints, and token ids. - OpenAI compatibility updates: expose new constrained_decoding backend selection via the compatibility shim; keep prior default behavior but allow customers to opt-in to 'cfg' or 'tokenizer_regex' backends through the API param constrained_backend. - Tests and fuzzing: extensive unit tests, integration tests against real model tokenizers (gpt-*-like BPE), and a new fuzz harness that found several edgecases (fixed). - Docs: updated structured-output guide with examples for CFG, regex, and tokenizer-aware constraints, plus migration notes for existing constraint sets. Compatibility: Default behavior preserved for existing customers. New backends are opt-in via the API param constrained_backend. Migration notes are in docs/structured-output.md. Performance: regex_backend (Rust) shows ~1.8x throughput vs the old matcher on long constraints in microbenchmarks; cfg_backend has similar latency to previous matcher for typical grammar sizes. The tokenizer-aware matcher incurs modest overhead but prevents incorrect constraint acceptance/failure. Testing & CI: All unit and integration tests pass. Fuzz suite discovered and fixed 4 failure modes related to unicode combining characters and trailing-space anchors. Rollout: staged canary on Dedicated and Hosted (10% traffic) with metrics for structured-output correctness, latency, and token cost. Follow-ups: - ENG-2178: expose constraint compilation diagnostics (warnings for ambiguous grammars) - ENG-2203: add streaming-aware partial-match handling (current work-in-progress draft) - Docs: add cookbook examples for common CFG patterns Commits: - 9f3a2d1 feat(constrained-decoding): add pluggable backend interface and cfg_backend implementation - a7c4b55 feat(regex): token-aware regex backend (rust) and ffi bridge - 4b2e9d8 fix(tokenizer): handle leading/trailing space and unicode normalization in token aligner - d6f1a11 test(fuzz): add fuzz harness and reproduce tokenizer edgecases - b1c7f23 docs: structured-output guide, examples, and migration notes Changed files (high level): - runtime/constrained_decoding/backend_interface.py - runtime/constrained_decoding/cfg_backend.py - runtime/constrained_decoding/regex_backend.rs - runtime/tokenizer/token_align.py - runtime/tokenizer/bpe_edgecases.rs - sdk/openai_compat/struct_output_shim.py - docs/structured-output.md - tests/constrained_decoding/test_cfg.py - tests/constrained_decoding/test_regex_tokenizer.py - tests/fuzz/fuzz_tokenizer.py - integration/ci/pipeline.yml Review conversation (summary): - Daniel Kim: "Can you clarify the backwards compatibility guarantees and the default?" Author: "Default behavior unchanged; constrained_backend param is opt-in. Migration notes added to docs." - Priya Rao: "Regex backend looks great — did you evaluate pathological regexes (catastrophic DFA blowup)?" Author: "Yes: we cap compilation complexity and fallback to interpreter with a warning; noted in docs and added a test." - Liam O'Connor: "Tokenizer mapping code seems complex; consider moving to runtime/tokenizer util and adding benchmarks." Author: "Moved to token_align.py, added microbenchmarks and comments." - Marisol Vega: "Please add clarity around merge/fallback strategy for streaming partial matches." Author: "Added follow-up ENG-2203; streaming partial-match handling remains a draft to avoid blocking this fix." CI summary: - unit-tests: pass - integration-tests: pass - lint: pass - fuzz-tests: pass (after re-run) - benchmarks: pass (microbench, regex_backend faster on long patterns) Merge: squashed and merged to main. Release notes: "Added pluggable constrained-decoding backends: CFG and token-aware regex matcher; fixed tokenizer edgecases that previously caused structured-output failures. Backends are opt-in via constrained_backend param; see docs/structured-output.md for migration steps."
